evidence.paraphrase: The filmmaker contrasts the mythic 'wild West' of stories with his claim that it doesn't really exist.
evidence.quote: The West," says he, "is the bunk. There ain\u2019t none such.

evidence.paraphrase: The stranger contrasts the fictional West depicted by writers with his failure to find it in reality.
evidence.quote:
Wild," says he. "Wild like the writers tell us about. The kind of a
West that Buffalo Bill knew. I\u2019ve hunted for it loud and long, but she
ain\u2019t and that\u2019s an end to it.

evidence.paraphrase: The filmmaker describes himself as a realist who dislikes artificiality.
evidence.quote: I am a realist," says he, dreamy-like. "I hate the artificial.

evidence.paraphrase: Waldemar explains his aim to capture authentic, real-life Western events for his moving picture.
evidence.quote:
I want realism. I want the spirit of the old West in it. I want a stage
hold-up, a bank robbery, with real people in it, in a Western town\u2014real
West.

evidence.paraphrase: Waldemar clarifies that he takes moving pictures.
Dirty reacts with unfamiliarity and curiosity about how moving pictures work.
evidence.quote: Does them pitchers make yuh think they\u2019re movin\u2019?

evidence.paraphrase: Waldemar explains the technical setup of the camera to film the staged robbery.
evidence.quote:
in the morning we\u2019ll
set up the camera in the hotel window which will give me a full shot at
the street, with the bank in the foreground

evidence.paraphrase: Waldemar reacts with dismay after nearly being hanged for the staged film stunt.
evidence.quote:
I seen you. I got a hundred feet of
the best hold-up on earth, and they were going to hang me.

evidence.paraphrase: Dirty angrily dismisses Waldemar and his film-making.
evidence.quote:
you can take your \u2014\u2014 creepin\u2019
tintypes and go plumb to \u2014\u2014!

evidence.paraphrase: Waldemar notes that an actual bank robbery occurred though the narrators did not commit it.
